PullRequest.Title: automations: feat: backport templates and target selection to 1.137
PullRequest.Body:
## Cherry-pick

Cherry-picks #334836 into `release/1.137`.

- Source commit: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6d68fbe0a37b57967e1efa6bf19c24de9fa39b5
- One signed cherry-pick commit with `-x` provenance.
- Rebased onto release commit `15903dfbe84cb7bea8a802624812043da8f3d9ba` after #334944 brought in the overlapping catalogue-state dependency.
- Resolved the two test-file conflicts by keeping the release's combined emissions assertion and error-recovery coverage, while retaining the additional local-operation, legacy-readability, and atomic-transition tests.
- Reuses the release's catalogue/store implementations unchanged. The remaining PR changes 18 files; the template and dialog UI are unchanged from the original cherry-pick.
- The provider-owned session-template prerequisite is already in this release through #334831.

## What this brings to 1.137

- **Starter automation templates:** editable issue-triage, pull-request-review, dependency-audit, and release-notes suggestions. Selecting a template opens the normal dialog; it does not create or schedule an automation.
- **Explicit targets:** new automations no longer silently inherit a recent GitHub workspace and appear locked to Cloud. Users choose a workspace or **No workspace** first. Single-agent targets explain the restriction and offer **Choose Workspace**; saved edit/duplicate targets and opaque provider configuration remain preserved.
- **Honest catalogue presentation:** use the release's existing `loading`, `ready`, `unavailable`, and `error` states in the UI, accessible content, and `listAutomations`. Known automations and usable local targets remain available when a remote provider is offline. Only `ready` may claim that an empty catalogue means no automations.
- **Regression coverage and focus safeguards:** retain the release's migration/readability safeguards, add coverage for unavailable providers and atomic transitions, keep full-text template hovers, and preserve focus without stealing it after delayed updates.

Provider ownership, workspace trust, managed policy, and existing AI feature gating are unchanged. There are no dependency or persistence-schema changes.

## Release validation

- [x] **177 targeted Electron tests passed after the rebase:** aggregate providers, Agent Host automation stores, New badge eligibility, and the Automations view.
- [x] Client type checking passed after the rebase.
- [x] Targeted ESLint passed for both resolved test files.
- [x] Verified unchanged upstream catalogue/store implementations and unchanged template/dialog UI, a signed single commit, a clean worktree, and no whitespace errors.

The original conflict-free cherry-pick had an identical stable patch ID to the source commit and passed 400 targeted Electron tests, including the dialog and workspace/agent pickers. The source PR also passed its full GitHub CI and completed Copilot review without findings. CI will rerun for the rebased head.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and updating the Automations view with empty, partial, loading, unavailable, error, or populated catalogues
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The view synchronously reads the in-memory automations array and catalogue state, reconciles persistent cards, toggles one state container, and renders four fixed templates only once when empty. Provider discovery/catalogue retrieval is already in flight and is not awaited to render the current state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the authoritative Agent Host automation catalogue snapshot and updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one subscription/initialization stream per registered Agent Host provider; the changed view only observes aggregate in-memory state and issues no boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider catalogue loading and updates already occurred independently of this view change; the prior view consumed only the aggregate automation rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the changed render critical path: the view immediately displays loading/partial state and reacts when existing provider work emits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of saved automations A and provider state transitions P. Card reconciliation is O(A) per distinct aggregate emission; templates and state containers are fixed-size and one-time. Realistic P is connection/setup transitions rather than frame-rate activity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI observable reactions execute serially on each distinct catalogue/automation emission. Provider catalogues may initialize independently, but the diff adds no new fan-out or polling; each state emission causes one bounded reconciliation pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cards remain cached by stable automation ID and are updated only when descriptor identity changes. Empty/template/state DOM is retained and reused. No cache keys, negative caching, or remote cache lifecycle changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the autorun, persistent-card maps, one-time template guards, and provider aggregate state derivation were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Automation catalogues can vary in size, but the added state transitions are infrequent and the changed work does not add boundary calls or reconstruct existing cards.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new state emissions can add an O(A) in-memory reconciliation on infrequent provider transitions, but cards are persistent, unchanged descriptors are skipped, and no I/O or repeated DOM reconstruction is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a new automation from a starter template, selecting a target, and confirming creation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Template selection synchronously opens the existing dialog with fixed prefilled text. The target hint recomputes available session types by synchronously enumerating registered providers. No automation is created until the user confirms; confirmation then follows the existing single create operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist or dispatch one automation creation to its selected provider after explicit confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one create call per confirmed dialog; selecting a template alone performs zero boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing Create Automation button opened the same dialog and issued the same single provider create call after confirmation. The template only supplies initial name, prompt, and schedule.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation completion is awaited after confirmation, as in the existing Create Automation flow; it is not on the template-selection/open-dialog critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed four templates; target hint work scales with registered provider/session-type count, normally small, and runs only on target/type selection changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One dialog and at most one create operation per user confirmation. Session-type hint recomputation is serialized by observable autoruns and has no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The four template nodes and eight managed hovers are created once per widget lifetime and disposed with the widget. Session-type availability comes from the existing provider registry; no cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: template click, dialog lifecycle, hint autorun, provider enumeration, and create routing were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count can vary, but enumeration is synchronous in-memory work already performed by the session-type picker, and the added hint repeats it only on low-frequency dialog events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new path is fixed-size, user-triggered, and reuses the existing one-create boundary without increasing cardinality or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the automation dialog without an explicit target and changing workspace or agent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog now leaves new automations target-less, hides target-dependent controls, and computes guidance from registered session types. Workspace restoration is disabled, so no recent workspace is implicitly selected; target-dependent configuration begins only after user selection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered provider/session-type count and low-frequency user target changes; no collection-wide remote operation is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker and hint observable reactions are serialized. The change does not start parallel provider requests and in practice defers existing target-dependent draft/configuration work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing picker/provider registry data is reused. Disabling restoration avoids consuming a cached recent workspace as an implicit target but does not add a new cache or miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: target-less initialization, restoration guard, control visibility, and synchronous provider enumeration were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of provider-specific configuration after explicit target selection varies, but that boundary is pre-existing and is deferred rather than newly made eager.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the changed default removes implicit target work and adds only bounded DOM/text updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling or moving focus inside Sessions custom views
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Wheel scrolling updates the existing Scrollable model and DOM. The new native scroll listener mirrors browser-driven scrollTop into that model; programmatic wheel updates immediately short-circuit because the model already equals the DOM value. Focus-in schedules one next-frame synchronization to capture browser focus auto-scroll.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll/focus event frequency. Each added event performs constant-time scroll-position validation; unchanged positions return before scrollbar rendering, while actual browser-driven focus scroll causes one scrollbar update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll events are handled serially. Focus synchronization is coalesced through a MutableDisposable so a newer focus-in cancels the prior scheduled frame callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retained collection is involved. Listener and scheduled callback ownership are disposed with CustomViewNode.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: DOM scroll wiring, Scrollable._setState equality guard, scrollbar render path, and callback disposal were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Scroll event rates vary by input device, but the equality guard in Scrollable prevents duplicate render work for the common programmatic-scroll feedback event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous UI regression. The hot-path hook is constant-time and duplicate programmatic notifications short-circuit before rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoking listAutomations and opening the Automations accessible view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: listAutomations reads existing in-memory rows and serializes the same array with one additional catalogueState field. Accessible content formats each available automation/run and appends four fixed template descriptions when empty.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Serialization/content generation remains O(A + R), where A is available automations and R is visible runs; the diff adds constant-size state/template output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both operations are synchronous per explicit invocation with no spawned work or parallel boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or invalidated. Both outputs are generated on demand as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: output construction and content loops were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large catalogues/history increase pre-existing serialization cost, but the diff adds only a constant enum field and four fixed template lines.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable serialization or allocation regression; asymptotic cost and invocation frequency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and all paginated diff pages. Traced view rendering, catalogue-state emissions, template/dialog creation, provider routing, accessibility/tool serialization, and custom scroll synchronization. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
